description: The >>PROPAGATE { ON | OFF } compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.21) - automatic propagation of an unhandled exception condition to the activating runtime element. Recognized and operand-validated by PropagateDirectiveProcessor (the runtime propagation effect is the deferred PHASE-13 EC work); the introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002 through the ONE ConstructRegistry funnel - it emitted a bespoke COBOL0883 until kb/Work PB725, which left COBOL0883 owning only the malformed-operand half. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.17.2 SR1: 'A PROPAGATE directive shall not be specified within a compilation unit'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 29: 'to cause propagation of an exception condition to an activating runtime element'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.18: 'The PROPAGATE directive is used to cause propagation of exception conditions to the activating runtime element') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.21.1).

directivePlacement.text: A PROPAGATE directive shall not be specified within a compilation unit

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.21.2 general format: PROPAGATE and OFF are underlined, ON is not, so per §2023:5.2.3 the ON alternative may be selected with the word omitted; §2023:7.3.21.4 GR4's OFF default is about omitting the DIRECTIVE, not about which alternative the format implies.

source:
>>PROPAGATE ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725PR.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
